title: Michigan November final: sentiment 51.5 (preliminary 51.0, October 48.0); year-ahead inflation expectations 3.7% (preliminary 4.3%, October 4.7%); long-run 3.3% (preliminary 3.4%, October 3.5%); current conditions revised down to 49.4 from 51.0, expectations up to 52.9 from 50.9; interviews October 20 to November 16
body:
# University of Michigan, November final (released Fri Nov 20 10:00 ET, read at the issuer)

| Index | Nov final | Nov prelim (card 20261106-049) | Oct | Nov 2025 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sentiment | 51.5 | 51.0 | 48.0 | 51.0 |
| Current conditions | 49.4 | 51.0 | 46.7 | 51.1 |
| Expectations | 52.9 | 50.9 | 48.8 | 51.0 |

**Inflation expectations:** year-ahead median 3.7% (preliminary 4.3%, October 4.7%; the director: 'plunged'), still above February's 3.4% and all 2024 readings. Long-run 3.3% (preliminary 3.4%, October 3.5%), above the 2024 range of 2.8% to 3.2%.

**Director's text (Joanne Hsu, issuer page):** gains 'led by substantial post-election gains in both short- and long-run expected business conditions'; personal finances improved for low- and middle-wealth consumers with falling gas prices; 'those with the largest stockholdings reported a decline in personal finances, consistent with continued AI-related agitation in stock markets'; expectations surged for independents, rose for Democrats, fell for Republicans; sentiment 9% below February. Consumers still say inflation, not unemployment, will cause greater hardship.

**Limit:** interviews ran October 20 to November 16, so they end before this week's AI selloff (cards 20261119-017 and 20261120-001). The final's revision is mostly in expectations and in year-ahead inflation.

**Registered:** CARL's V12 long-run trigger (below 3.0%): not met at 3.3%. No WALTER-scanned threshold keys this series.
